# Copilot Code Review Guidelines for Stepper-C

**Purpose:** Code review guidelines for pull requests to Stepper-C, a hardware- and
OS-agnostic closed-loop stepper motor control library for embedded systems, developed
under **MISRA C:2012** (with Amendments 1-3).

---

## 1. Scope of the library

- The library implements current control (PI per phase, back-EMF feed-forward,
  anti-windup, bus voltage compensation), microstepping, a trapezoidal motion
  planner, the voltage limit and duty cycles of two power stage topologies (full
  bridge, shared leg) and protection trips.
- Timer, PWM and ADC drivers, interrupt setup, encoders, homing, communication and
  application logic belong to the firmware that uses the library, not here.
- Hardware is reached only through the callbacks of `struct sstep_callbacks`.

## 2. Hard rules (block the PR)

- Library sources (`src/`, `inc/`, `sstep.h`) include only `<stddef.h>`,
  `<stdint.h>`, `<stdbool.h>` and SSTEP headers.
- No dynamic memory, no RTOS calls, no driver headers, no global or static mutable
  data, no recursion.
- `sstep.h` and `inc/` contain the public API only. Internal types, macros and
  `static inline` helpers stay in `src/`; a public header never includes a header
  from `src/`. `struct sstep` stays opaque; the state is accessed only through
  `sstep_ctx_of()`.
- A change of `struct sstep_ctx` updates `SSTEP_STATE_BYTES` in `inc/sstep_ctrl.h`.
- Every arithmetic change works with both numeric backends (fixed point and float).
- Public symbols use the `sstep_` / `SSTEP_` prefix; public headers keep the
  `extern "C"` guards and a Doxygen comment for every public item.
- The code compiles without warnings with
  `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion`, also for Cortex-M.
- `clang-format` (repository `.clang-format`) reports no changes.
- Every behavior change comes with a GoogleTest unit test; a change of the control
  behavior also with a closed-loop test on the motor model
  (`tests/unit/gtest_sstep_loop.cpp`).
- Line and branch coverage of `src/` stays at 100 % in both backends (the
  `coverage` target fails below `SSTEP_COVERAGE_MIN`).
- `misra-analyze` reports 0 violations; an unavoidable one needs an entry in
  the deviation register in `docs/misra.md`.

## 3. MISRA C:2012 review focus

Run `cmake --build <build-dir> --target misra-analyze`; it fails on any
violation. A PR must not add violations without a documented deviation
(rule, location, rationale, approval) in `docs/misra.md`. The addon does not
check the directives; review those by hand (see the manual review notes in
`docs/misra.md`).

| Area | Rules | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language | 1.4 | No `_Alignof`, `_Generic`, `_Noreturn`, `_Atomic`, `_Thread_local` |
| Essential types | 10.1-10.8 | No implicit narrowing or signedness change; explicit casts on composite expressions |
| Pointer casts | 11.3, 11.5 | Only the two DEV-01 casts in `sstep_ctx_of()` / `sstep_ctx_of_const()` |
| Expressions | 12.1, 12.2 | Explicit parentheses on mixed-precedence expressions; shift amount within type width; signed shifts through `sstep_asr()` |
| Side effects | 13.2, 13.3, 13.5 | `++`/`--` not mixed with other side effects; no side effects in `&&`/`||` right operands |
| Control flow | 14.4, 15.5, 15.6, 15.7 | Boolean controlling expressions; single point of exit; compound statements; `else` after `else if` |
| Switch | 16.1-16.7 | Well-formed `switch`, `default` present, `break` on every clause |
| Functions | 8.3, 17.2, 17.7, 17.8 | Same parameter names in declaration and definition; no recursion; return values used or cast to `void`; parameters not modified |
| Pointers and arrays | 18.1, 18.4 | Index within bounds; no pointer arithmetic beyond array indexing |
| Preprocessor | 20.7, 20.9 | Macro parameters parenthesized; only defined identifiers in `#if` |
| Standard library | 21.3, 21.6 | No `malloc`/`free`; no stdio in library code |
| Declarations | 8.4, 8.7, 8.13 | Compatible prior declaration for external functions; `static` where possible; `const` pointers where possible |

## 4. Embedded considerations

- State lives in the caller-owned `struct sstep`; sizes are fixed at build time by
  `inc/sstep_config.h` and `SSTEP_STATE_BYTES`.
- `sstep_fast_loop()` runs in the PWM/ADC interrupt: its execution time must stay
  bounded (no loops over data, only loops with fixed limits); flag anything that adds
  work or stack to it.
- `sstep_slow_loop()` and the commands run in one task context; the hand-off to the
  fast loop is a lock-free double buffer that relies on single-core preemption. Do
  not add hidden locking or calls from other contexts; only `sstep_report_fault()`
  may be called from an interrupt.
- Callbacks run in the context of the function that calls them; `pwm_write()` and
  `on_fault()` may run in the interrupt.
- Update the stack table in `docs/configuration.md` when a function's frame changes.

## 5. Documentation

Update `README.md`, `docs/motor-control.md` (control algorithms and measured
results), `docs/usage.md`, `docs/integration.md` and `docs/api.md` together with any
API or behavior change. Every number in the documentation is measured; re-measure
the stack table, the memory footprint and the closed-loop results when they can
change.

Every user-visible change gets an entry under `[Unreleased]` in
`CHANGELOG.md`. The public API is stable within a major version (Semantic
Versioning): flag any removed or changed public symbol, struct member or
return value.
